newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SLIGHTLY FIRMER ON U.S. UNIT.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SLIGHTLY FIRMER ON U.S. UNIT.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted slightly firmer on the U.S. dollar on Tuesday morning after a rapid decline which began last Wednesday but dealers expected it to slip again on the back of a big import payment coming up later in the day.

"The market is still in shambles so to speak although people have narrowed down their spreads a bit. I think there's still pressure for the dollar to depreciate further," one dealer said, adding that most players were stocking up in anticipation of the big import order.
"We can only tell where the dollar is going to go after the payment," he said.

Dealers said the dollar's free fall, prompted by another large import order on Wednesday which left the market Z$80 million short, was intensified on Friday by Reserve Bank governor Leonard Tsumba's statements published in a local paper that the local unit was overvalued by some five percent.
He hinted that the bank would allow it to depreciate further in order to maintain export competivemess.

At around 0800 GMT on Tuesday, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.5000/6000 on the U.S. dollar, slightly firmer compared to 11.5200/6500 late Monday and was at 18.7750/9500 from 18.9320/9690 versus sterling.
It however eased to 6.2650/3000 from 6.2440/2565 against the mark and to 2.5475/5500 against South Africa's rand from 2.5200/5275.
